assertion.name: Rickettsia conorii
assertion.description: Agent of Mediterranean spotted fever (boutonneuse fever) and, through its subspecies indica, israelensis and caspia, of Indian tick typhus, Israeli spotted fever and Astrakhan fever.

selected_evidence.snippet: Although homogeneous genotypically, strains within the R. conorii species show MST genotypic, serotypic, and epidemio-clinical dissimilarities.

assertion.name: Spotted fever group Rickettsia
assertion.description: The taxon that defines this disease group. SFG rickettsiae are obligately intracytosolic Gram-negative bacteria that cycle between an arthropod vector and a vertebrate host and that share an endothelial tropism in humans. Membership of this clade — not the identity of the arthropod, and not the geography of the disease name — is the unifying criterion for the entries grouped here.

selected_evidence.snippet: Several species of tick-borne rickettsiae that were considered nonpathogenic for decades are now associated with human infections, and novel Rickettsia species of undetermined pathogenicity continue to be detected in or isolated from ticks around the world.

assertion.name: Rickettsia australis
assertion.description: Agent of Queensland tick typhus in eastern Australia. Like R. akari it has been assigned to the transitional group on genomic grounds while remaining a spotted fever group infection clinically.

selected_evidence.snippet: Rickettsia australis, the etiologic agent of Queensland tick typhus (QTT), is increasingly being recognized as a cause of community-acquired acute febrile illness in eastern Australia.

assertion.name: Rickettsia akari
assertion.description: Agent of rickettsialpox, transmitted by the house mouse mite rather than a tick. Historically classified within the spotted fever group and still grouped with it clinically and serologically, but reassigned to the transitional group on genomic grounds.

selected_evidence.snippet: R. akari was initially classified as a member of the spotted fever group (SFG) of rickettsia, but it is now placed in the transitional group, which has features of both the spotted fever group and the typhus group (TG) of rickettsiae.

assertion.name: Rickettsia africae
assertion.description: Agent of African tick-bite fever; a mild, self-limiting member of the group that provokes a markedly weaker endothelial inflammatory response than R. conorii.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mediterranean spotted fever (MSF) caused by Rickettsia conorii (R. conorii) is a potential lethal disease while African tick bite fever (ATBF) caused by Rickettsia africae is a self-limiting flu-like illness.

assertion.name: Rickettsia rickettsii
assertion.description: Agent of Rocky Mountain spotted fever in North America and of Brazilian spotted fever in South America; the most virulent member of the group.

selected_evidence.snippet: Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF) is a life-threatening disease caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, an obligately intracellular bacterium that is spread to human beings by ticks.

selected_evidence.snippet: Tick-borne rickettsioses are caused by obligate intracellular bacteria belonging to the spotted fever group of the genus Rickettsia.

assertion.name: Rickettsia sibirica subsp. sibirica
assertion.description: Agent of North Asian (Siberian) tick typhus across Siberia, Mongolia, Kazakhstan and eastern China.

selected_evidence.snippet: Rickettsia sibirica sibirica is the causative agent of Siberian or North Asian tick typhus, a tick-borne rickettsiosis known to exist in Siberia and eastern China.

assertion.name: Poliovirus

infectious_agent_term.description: Left unbound deliberately. NCBITaxon has no species-level "Poliovirus" node: it carries only serotype terms (NCBITaxon:12080 Poliovirus 1, NCBITaxon:12083 Poliovirus 2, NCBITaxon:12086 Poliovirus 3) plus strain-level descendants, and the species-level parent NCBITaxon:138950 "Enterovirus C" also contains the coxsackie A viruses and is therefore too broad. Because paralytic poliomyelitis is caused by all three serotypes, no single serotype term fits either. The has_subtypes entries below divide the agent on the WPV-versus-VDPV origin axis rather than by serotype, so the serotype terms do not fit there either and are deliberately left unbound throughout.

assertion.description: Poliovirus circulates as two epidemiologically distinct forms relevant to global eradication. Wild poliovirus (WPV, serotypes 1-3) is the naturally circulating virus targeted for eradication. Vaccine-derived poliovirus (VDPV) instead arises when the live attenuated oral poliovirus vaccine (OPV) replicates for a prolonged period in an under-vaccinated community and reverts toward wild-type neurovirulence and transmissibility, producing paralytic disease clinically indistinguishable from WPV infection. VDPVs are further divided by the setting in which that reversion occurred: circulating VDPV (cVDPV) sustains person-to-person transmission in an under-vaccinated community, immunodeficiency-associated VDPV (iVDPV) arises from prolonged replication in a person with a B-cell immunodeficiency, and ambiguous VDPV (aVDPV) covers isolates that fit neither. cVDPV is the form that drives outbreaks and is the target of monovalent OPV2 response campaigns.

has_subtypes.name: WPV
has_subtypes.description: The naturally circulating, non-vaccine-derived virus targeted for global eradication. Wild serotypes 2 and 3 have been certified eradicated; WPV1 remains endemic in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

has_subtypes.name: VDPV
has_subtypes.description: Virus descended from the live attenuated OPV strains that has reverted toward wild-type neurovirulence and transmissibility during prolonged replication. Genetically identified by divergence from the parent Sabin strain in the VP1 capsid-coding region. The circulating subform (cVDPV) is the outbreak-driving form; VDPV2 is the serotype responsible for the majority of contemporary cVDPV outbreaks.

selected_evidence.snippet: VDPVs can emerge when live, attenuated OPV is administered in a community with low vaccination coverage. Replication of OPV in a person who was recently vaccinated can result in viral reversion to neurovirulence, which can cause paralytic poliomyelitis in unvaccinated persons who are exposed to the vaccine-derived virus.

assertion.name: Varicella-zoster virus
assertion.description: VZV (human herpesvirus 3) is a neurotropic alphaherpesvirus with a biphasic lifecycle comprising lytic infection in permissive tissues and latent infection in sensory ganglia. VZV encodes immune evasion proteins (ORF61p, ORF47p, IE-62) that antagonize type I interferon signaling, and envelope glycoproteins (gB, gE, gH/gL, gI, gM) that mediate cell-to-cell spread and skin tropism. During latency, transcription is restricted to VZV latency-associated transcripts (VLTs) and VLT-ORF63 fusion transcripts.

selected_evidence.snippet: Our large scanning analysis identifies and subsequent experiments confirm 200 VZV circRNAs.

During latency, transcription is restricted to VZV latency-associated transcripts (VLTs) and VLT-ORF63 fusion transcripts.

assertion.description: A positive-strand RNA virus of the family Hepeviridae. assertion.name: New World orthohantaviruses
assertion.description: Rodent-borne New World orthohantaviruses, including Sin Nombre virus and Andes virus, cause hantavirus pulmonary/cardiopulmonary syndrome after zoonotic respiratory exposure. "New World orthohantaviruses" is a geographical grouping of the American species rather than a taxon, so the binding here is the genus Orthohantavirus and the preferred_term carries the narrower sense. It is present in essentially all cases of BV and is the organism that forms the adherent biofilm, but it is also carried by a minority of asymptomatic women, so its presence is necessary rather than sufficient for the syndrome.

selected_evidence.snippet: is present in essentially all cases of BV but can also be detected in a minority of asymptomatic women

assertion.name: Prevotella timonensis
assertion.description: An anaerobe of the BV consortium, reclassified as Hoylesella timonensis. It adheres to vaginal and endocervical epithelium as strongly as Gardnerella but provokes less of a proinflammatory epithelial response, and it carries an unusually large complement of mucus-degrading fucosidases and sialidases. It is curated here because the barrier-degrading arm of this entry is not a Gardnerella monopoly. The `term:` binds the current NCBI taxonomy name, Hoylesella timonensis; the literature cited here, including the 2024 papers, still writes Prevotella timonensis, which is retained as the preferred term.

selected_evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that P. timonensis, but not P. bivia, strongly adheres to vaginal and endocervical cells to a similar level as G. vaginalis but did not elicit a comparable proinflammatory epithelial response.

assertion.name: Campylobacter jejuni
assertion.description: The bacterial species most convincingly associated with alpha-HCD/IPSID. Helicobacter pylori and intestinal parasites (including Giardia) have also been reported. No organism has been shown to be necessary or sufficient.

selected_evidence.snippet: These results indicate that campylobacter and immunoproliferative small intestinal disease are associated and that C. jejuni should be added to the growing list of human pathogens responsible for immunoproliferative states.

assertion.name: Helicobacter pylori
assertion.description: A second bacterium reported in association with alpha-HCD/IPSID, by analogy with its established role in gastric MALT lymphoma. The evidence is weaker than for C. jejuni and amounts to co-detection rather than a demonstrated causal role.

selected_evidence.snippet: Campylobacter jejuni or Helicobacter pylori) can be associated.
